title: The Wolf and the Lamb
source: Aesop's Fables, tr. G. F. Townsend (1867), 'The Wolf and the Lamb'
lesson: A bully will always find a reason.
lines: A wolf spotted a lamb drinking at a stream. He wanted lunch, but first he wanted an excuse.
You're muddying my water! growled the wolf, stomping up with a very serious face and a very silly excuse.
But sir, said the lamb, I'm downstream from you. The water flows from you to me.
Well, you insulted me last year! I wasn't even born last year.
Then it was your father! The wolf was running out of excuses, fast. He even checked his notes.
He gave up arguing, and pounced anyway. Which, honestly, is what he planned all along.
A bully will always find a reason. Don't waste your time arguing with someone who has already decided. Stay away from them, and stay safe.
Next episode: quarrelling brothers and a bundle of sticks. Follow so you don't miss it!
